selected_passages.text: The second day of the Sam Bankman-Fried trial featured starkly contrasting opening statements where prosecutors painted him as a liar who stole billions for a lavish lifestyle, while his defense argued he was a good-faith startup founder who acted innovatively and was willing to make customers whole. The proceedings included testimony from a victim, a former friend who admitted to writing code contributing to a crime, and the upcoming appearance of key witnesses like Gary Wang and Matt Huang, setting the stage for the jury to determine the nature of Bankman-Fried's actions.

selected_passages.title: sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand
selected_passages.text:
- Prosecutors alleged Bankman-Fried stole customer funds to finance his lifestyle, political donations, and risky bets through Alameda Research.
- Defense attorneys argued Bankman-Fried acted in good faith, built successful businesses, and did not defraud anyone.
- Witnesses include a victim who lost nearly $100,000, a former friend who admitted to unwittingly writing criminal code, and upcoming star witness Gary Wang.
- The trial highlights the debate over whether Bankman-Fried was a 'man' who lied or a 'boy' who made mistakes in a high-risk startup environment.
- Key figures like Caroline Ellison, Damian Williams, and venture capital partners are expected to provide further insight into the alleged scheme.

[sources/Is_Sam_Bankman-Fried_a_bad_man_or_a_good_boy_Lawyers_swap_opening_statements_before_first_witnesses_take_the_stand]
The second day of the Sam Bankman-Fried trial featured starkly contrasting opening statements where prosecutors painted him as a liar who stole billions for a lavish lifestyle, while his defense argued he was a good-faith startup founder who acted innovatively and was willing to make customers whole.
